mitre_mapping.description: Adversaries may delete or disable system recovery features to make remediation harder during ransomware execution.
Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability and demand ransom payments.
Adversaries abuse PowerShell commands and scripts to execute malicious code and stagers.
Adversaries exploit weaknesses or vulnerabilities in Internet-facing programs to gain initial network access.

mitre_mapping.technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
mitre_mapping.description: Adversaries clear security and system event logs to evade detection and hinder forensic analysis.

kill_chain.kill_chain_status: Critical Stage - Active Threat Impact / Ransomware Execution

stages.name: 1. Initial Access & Delivery
stages.description: Adversary achieves initial foothold through phishing, exploit public application, or external authentication.

stages.name: 2. Execution & Staging
stages.description: Execution of malicious scripts, obfuscated PowerShell, or secondary droppers.

stages.name: 3. Persistence & Privilege Escalation
stages.description: Establishing persistent autostart registry keys, scheduled tasks, or acquiring administrator tokens.

stages.name: 4. Credential Access & Discovery
stages.description: Dumping memory credentials, LSASS tampering, SAM extraction, or network enumeration.

stages.name: 5. Command & Control (C2)
stages.description: Maintaining outbound communication channels, beaconing, or DNS tunnels to remote servers.

stages.name: 6. Impact & Extortion
stages.description: System inhibition, volume shadow copy deletion, mass file encryption, and ransom extortion.

flagged_threats.description: Network traffic destined for known backdoor/C2 port 8443 (HTTPS Alternate C2 Gateway).

threat_classification.narrative: Critical threat indicators show active ransomware staging, shadow copy deletion, or data encryption extortion artifacts.

recommendations.threat_summary: Based on risk score (100/100) and detected Ransomware / Extortion, the AI recommendation engine suggests the following containment and forensic steps:

containment_actions.action: Block 2 malicious external IP(s) on perimeter firewall and EDR.
Immediately disconnect host from corporate LAN and Wi-Fi to prevent lateral encryption spreading.
Check offline immutable backups and verify integrity of VSS shadow copies on unaffected systems.
Audit and remove unauthorized Windows Registry Run keys, Scheduled Tasks, and anomalous startup services.

investigation_checklist: Inspect Master File Table ($MFT) and USN Journal for mass file renaming activity.
Identify initial access vector (Phishing email, RDP brute force, or unpatched VPN/firewall).
Inspect AutoRuns / WMI event subscriptions for disguised binaries.
Preserve full volatile memory dump (.raw/.dmp) using WinPmem or FTK Imager prior to power down.
Generate and record SHA-256 cryptographic hashes for all acquired disk artifacts.
Submit extracted malicious file hashes to internal Threat Intelligence (MISP / VirusTotal).
